answer.text: Ba's words: "if it not public api let's check through browser and let's see what api for get, for apply and so on, then you can get my personal account token to call their api no need to go through user interface, just in case it hard then interface as fallback". Confirmed approach: research each board's public API first; where none exists, find the internal web API the site itself calls (observed through the browser) for listing jobs, job detail, apply and similar, and call it with Ba's own account token (kept in local secret storage, never in the repo); the browser UI is the fallback only when the API path is too hard. Research should document both get and apply endpoints and flag terms-of-use and account-restriction risk per board (e.g. LinkedIn). This run builds read-only research; applying through APIs stays out of scope for now and will be a separate change request after Ba sees the research findings.

Ba's words: "For example the requirement ask for Redux but my skill have ReactJs, NextJs then you can update redux in cv to match with requirement because that is the real fact that need to have." Confirmed: implied skills from well-known implications (e.g. Redux from React/Next.js) are added automatically as derived facts with an 'Implied from f-x' label showing the cited facts, and Undo. Numbers, years of experience and durations are never changed or invented: they always come from Ba's real master facts (Ba also asked about stretching years to match a JD, e.g. '3 years React/Next/Node'; that was declined as misrepresentation, and Ba will correct the master CV if the real duration is longer). Hold G1: revise the spec to this answer and E-1, then Ba approves the revised spec.

data.note: Revise the spec to Ba's answers to E-1 and E-2, then Ba approves the revised version. E-1: research public APIs per board first; where none exists, the board's internal web API (found by observing the site in the browser) called with Ba's own account token stored in local secret storage; browser UI only as fallback. Research documents get and apply endpoints and terms-of-use/account risk per board; this run stays read-only (apply via API remains a non-goal, to be a later change request). E-2: replace REQ-16's strict rule: implied skills from well-known implications (e.g. Redux from React/Next.js) are auto-added as derived facts labelled with the facts they are implied from, with Undo. Numbers, years and durations are never changed or invented; they come only from real master facts.

escalation.detail:
The human asked (their words): "check more with this one, it auto lookback and optimize the cv with those rules". The attached image is a Vietnamese recruiter post (VNPT hiring) with a CV checklist for IT candidates. Its rules, translated:

1. Timeline: every Education and Experience entry gives month/year, e.g. "06/2023 – 08/2025: Software Developer", not "2023 – 2025".
2. Strongest experience first: put the experience most relevant to the position at the top; prioritise standout projects/work and the strongest tech stack; describe what you did, with which technology, and what result. Bad: "Participated in system development." Good: "06/2024 – 08/2025 | Backend Developer – Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL – built REST APIs and optimised the system, cutting response time by X%."
3. Concise, correct, scannable (recruiters spend seconds per CV): full and correct name, phone, email; LinkedIn/GitHub/portfolio if any; skills/tech stack relevant to the JD; education and certificates with month/year; 1–2 pages, easy layout; do not list many technologies without real experience.
Tip: a "10-second test": can a recruiter see the strongest experience, the tech stack and the fit for this position within 10 seconds?

Requested behaviour: after tailoring, the system automatically reviews ("looks back at") each tailored CV against these rules and revises it to satisfy them, without the human asking each time.

Constraint the change must keep (existing spec, REQ-27/REQ-28 and the derived-fact screen): rule 2's "result" numbers (e.g. "X%") may only come from facts Ba wrote; when a fact has no measured result, the CV must not invent one. Missing month/year dates or missing results should become a fact request to Ba, not invented values. Rule 3's "don't list technologies without real experience" should drop skills with no supporting fact.
escalation.question: Approve this change request? Add CV quality rules from a recruiter checklist (attached): the CV bot automatically reviews each tailored CV against them and fixes it before sending: month/year dates, most relevant experience first, did-what/with-what/result bullets, concise 1-2 pages.

answer.text: Approved, with a broader scope (human's words: "it a one rules collect some other HR can be have different opinion we need to research and auto optimize each time run for each job requirement"). The attached checklist is only one recruiter's opinion, not the rule set. Requirements: (1) research CV guidance from multiple HR/recruiter sources (other recruiters and employers may disagree) and build the CV quality rules from that collected research, keeping where each rule came from; (2) on every run, for each job, automatically review and optimize the tailored CV against those rules AND that job's own requirements (JD), so the emphasis and ordering can differ per job; (3) keep the existing truthfulness rules: no invented numbers, dates, employers, titles or skills; missing details become fact requests to Ba.
